answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by charging a time-locked berth fee at a public jetty of identity: each new account posts a bond that only unlocks after several epochs of graded work. Early payouts stay an ember—small, watched, and extinguished if peers find cloned answers or shared keys. By dawn of the vesting window, a unique work history has either earned the bond back or been slashed, so spinning thousands of shells becomes unprofitable rather than merely against the rules.
